Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Anton Khmelinskii in collaboration with Jan Padeken offers the following PhD project:
The progressive deterioration of protein homeostasis (proteostasis) is a primary hallmark of aging. As organisms age, the functionality of the proteostasis network, comprised of molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy, declines, leading to the accumulation of misfolded and aggregated proteins that compromise cellular viability. Proteostatic decline is not merely a consequence of aging but an early, causal event whereby loss of proteostasis precedes and predicts organismal decline, and its onset is sufficient to accelerate aging. Conversely, genetic or pharmacological enhancement of proteostasis network capacity can extend lifespan and suppresses age-related disease associated with protein misfolding across multiple model systems. These observations raise fundamental questions: what endogenous small molecules sustain proteostasis during aging, can their supplementation prevent neurodegenerative (and other protein folding diseases) and slow the aging process?

PhD project: Therapeutic applications of small molecule modulators of proteostasis

Organisms across all domains of life employ the accumulation of small organic osmolytes, which include molecules such as betaine and taurine, to mitigate proteotoxic stress. Recent work has also demonstrated anti-aging properties of this molecules, through yet unclear mechanisms. This project aims at dissecting the mode of action of different osmolytes using human cellular model systems and C. elegans as a model of organismal aging. We would like to address the following questions:

1. How do osmolytes affect cellular and organismal physiology?
2. Which types of stresses can be mitigated with exogenous osmolytes?
3. What types of protein misfolding pathologies (e.g., neurodegenerative diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Alzheimers's, Parkinson's, Huntington's) can be ameliorated with exogenous osmolytes?

The project is part of an ongoing collaboration between the Khmelinskii and Padeken groups, which gives you the opportunity to become an expert in a wide range of methods and experimental approaches. This includes transcriptomics, proteomics, cell and molecular biology, fluorescence microscopy and advanced high-throughput mutagenesis screening.

If you are interested in this project, please select Khmelinskii/Padeken as your group preference in the IPP application platform. Are you an ambitious scientist looking to push the boundaries of research while interacting with colleagues from multiple disciplines and cultures? Then joining the IPP is your opportunity to give your scientific career a flying start!
All you need is:

Master or equivalent
Interactive personality & good command of English
2 letters of reference

Exciting, interdisciplinary projects in a lively international environment, with English as our working language

Advanced training in scientific techniques and professional skills
Access to our state-of-the-art Core Facilities and their technical expertise

Fully funded positions with financing until the completion of your thesis
A lively community ofmore than 200 PhD students from 44 different countries

For more details on the projects offered and how to apply via the online form using the apply button.

The deadline for applications is 15 October 2026. Interviews will take place at IMB in Mainz on 18+19 January 2027.

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.8725 hours/week = 75%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Research associates (m/f/x) in scientific computing

The chair of numerical mathematics at the Ruhr University Bochum focuses on the development of efficient algorithms for solving problems in the natural and engineering sciences. A special emphasis is on hyperbolic conservation laws and high‑dimensional problems. We develop efficient numerical methods exploiting low‑rank tensor techniques and mixed‑precision algorithms. Moreover, we are interested in structure‑preserving numerical methods that are particularly adapted to the physical structure of the modeling equations, as well as in hybrid methods that couple models of different complexity for optimal efficiency. We are participating in the Collaborative Research Center on “Cosmic Interacting Matter” and are therefore especially interested in plasma‑physics applications in astrophysical environments as well as in magnetic‑confinement fusion. Recently, we have also turned to the Wetterich equation, an exact equation of the functional renormalization group, providing a systematic framework to study many‑body and field‑theoretic models such as classical and quantum phase transitions in solid‑state physics.

As a research assistant (m/f/x), you will independently develop new numerical schemes, implement and test their properties as well as analyze their numerical properties in challenging application problems. The opportunity to pursue further academic qualifications (a Ph.D.) is offered and encouraged.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 36
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-13

Your tasks:

- Research in scientific computing with the focus on the development and efficient implementation of numerical methods for hyperbolic differential equation
- Implementation of efficient algorithms for application problems
- Writing of papers for publication in highly ranked international journals
- Teaching in applied mathematics

Your profile:

- Applicants are expected to have an excellent degree, Master's or Diploma in a relevant academic field such as Mathematics, Computational Sciences, Physics when filling the position and at least a Bachelor's degree when applying.

jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation
- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.
- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.
- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.

Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage.

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

 Unit’s description and purpose: 

Global Products, Programs and Policy (GPPP) provides leadership to the Fairtrade system with selected product, program and policy intelligence. To this end GPPP provides information, tools and strategic direction as the main outputs. 

GPPP facilitates and contributes to coherent implementation of strategic plans within the Fairtrade system. GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The work will deliver measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The Cocoa Manager joins a team that works fluidly, sharing responsibilities across multiple workstreams supporting each other where the need is the greatest to achieve their objectives. The environment is dynamic and priorities can shift with external events impacting workplans.  

In addition to other duties the Cocoa Manager, working within GPPP cocoa, will  work in close collaboration with Producer Networks, National Fairtrade Organisations and the Fairtrade International Global Impact team responsible for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, to ensure the Fairer Futures Programme – West Africa Cocoa is implemented professionally and on time. The programme is primarily focused on increasing the household income of farmers who are members of Small Producer Organisaitons in the programme. The programme leads to farm level interventions through Small Producer Organisaitons including pruning, cocoa tree planting and shade tree planting among others. The programme includes further interventions on income such as Village Savings and Loans Association, and interventions on social compliance including increasing the effectiveness of child labour monitoring, reporting and remediation.

- Programme design. Work with stakeholders, and mostly importantly the Producer Network, to ensure programme design is based on evidence with robust monitoring, evaluation and learning contributing to the evolution of the programme.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant/Doctoral Student (f/m/d) - Chair of Behavioral Accounting (Research-Manager/in)
jobs.employer_name: WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management-1
jobs.description:
General informationThe new Chair of Behavioral Accounting ( Prof. Dr. Victor van Pel t) at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management in Vallendar is dedicated to the empirical and experimental analysis of decision-making behavior in accounting settings. The focus is on behavioral accounting, controlled, online, and field experiments, and contemporary trends like the use of artificial intelligence. Our research examines how controls, performance feedback, and reporting choices shape the judgments and decisions of managers, employees, investors, and other firm stakeholders. WHU has an international orientation, offers an excellent research environment, and has a vibrant doctoral programme. Moreover, our chair is part of the Finance and Accounting Group, which organizes frequent reading groups and research seminars that further strengthen your doctoral training. This position is particularly suited for people (f/m/d) interested in behavioral research, with a focus on accounting questions, and a career in academia.
Your mission Research
• Conducting independent research in the field of behavioral accounting, in particular on experimental issues in reporting, controls, performance feedback, and the use of artificial intelligence in accounting.
• The aim is to present research results at international conferences and publish them in leading journals.

Teaching
• Collaboration in the implementation and further development of courses in the field of financial and management accounting (e.g. preparation of materials, supervision of students, data analysis or support with experiments).
• Opportunity to gradually take on your own teaching responsibilities and further develop your teaching skills as part of your doctoral programme.

Doctoral programme
• Active participation in WHU’s structured doctoral programme, which includes methodological and theoretical courses, research seminars, and presentations in the doctoral colloquium.
• Use of the international research environment for professional and personal development, including access to laboratory and online recruitment resources and support for conference travel.

Your profileAcademic background
• Above-average master’s degree in accounting, economics, finance or a related area.
• Ideally, your master’s thesis was written in a subject area related to behavioral or experimental research.
• We particularly value if you’ve finished a preparation track, like a research master or another specialized graduate research program.

Technical and methodological skills
• Strong mathematical programming, analytical, and critical thinking skills.
• Experience with experimental design, statistical inference, and academic research and writing practices.
• Proficiency in at least one of the following statistical programming languages: R, Stata, or Python.
• Experience with oTree for conducting experiments is a big plus.

Research interests
• Strong interest in experimental behavioral research, particularly in the areas of accounting.
• Interest in topics such as misreporting, performance measurement and feedback, controls, incentives, and contemporary issues like sustainability and the use of AI is particularly welcome.

Personal requirements
• A passion for learning and scientific research in an international environment.
• Excellent written and spoken English proficiency (German proficiency is not required).

What we offer Academic Environment

WHU has more than 60 faculty members in the fields of management, finance and accounting, economics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing and sales, and supply chain management. Research at WHU aims to adhere to three principles: quality, internationality, and practical relevance.

WHU is an equal opportunity employer and thus welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds. We believe in the benefits of diversity and therefore foster an international, inclusive, and inspiring working environment.

ContactFor questions please contact:

Professor Victor van Pelt
email: Victor.vanPelt@whu.edu

Since its inception in 1984, we have driven excellence and entrepreneurial thinking, producing innovative research that steers progress for all areas of society and industry. At both the Vallendar and Düsseldorf campuses, we empower leaders to become responsible changemakers, guided by integrity, diversity, and strengthened by a deep sense of togetherness.

Job Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Our work has provided exciting insights into organellogenesis and enabled us to develop novel tools for dissecting the molecular and cellular biology of host-symbiont interactions (see e.g., Morales et al. (2023) Curr Biol. doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.020.; Sørensen et al. (2024) FEBS J. doi: 10.1111/febs.17356; Maurya et al. (2025) Science Adv. doi: 10.1126/sciadv.adp8518; Klimenko et al. (2025) Plant Phys. doi: 10.1093/plphys/kiaf504; Hammond et al. (2026) Nat Commun. doi: 10.1038/s41467-026-70084-0.). The successful candidate will contribute to a current project at the heart of our research program, with the opportunity to shape the project in part according to their scientific interests, expertise, and strengths. The position will also involve a limited amount of undergraduate teaching in German [4 contact hours (Semesterwochenstunden) per week], providing an opportunity to contribute to the training of the next generation of biologists.

State-of-the-art AI systems depend heavily on models, providers and hardware from the U.S. and China, which represents a big challenge of Europe’s sovereignty for AI model development and deployment (e.g., trustworthiness, dependability, performance, modularity). The Horizon Europe project OptimAIse (Optimising Performance and Trust for Integrity-driven Modular genAI Software Engineering) addresses these challenges by delivering a scalable, modular, and interoperable reference architecture that leverages European hardware to enable efficient and simplified large language model deployments. The SpiNNaker2 hardware, developed by TU Dresden and commercialized by SpiNNcloud, is one of Europe’s most promising alternatives for the energy-efficient serving of LLMs. SpiNNaker2 is a massively parallel architecture with locally dense compute and globally sparse and low-latency communication, ideal to realize efficient AI models by leveraging sparse and event-based computing.

The candidate will develop and adopt LLMs for the SpiNNaker2 hardware. The models shall be implemented on the hardware using an existing software stack and optimized with ML compilers such as MLIR. Besides applying known approaches such as Mixture-of-Experts, the candidate shall follow the state of the art of efficient language models and try novel approaches on SpiNNaker2. In addition, the work will derive requirements and recommendation for next-generation AI hardware such as Spinnaker3, thus guiding the future of efficient AI systems.
